answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with seizable sponsor bonds: a newcomer joins only when an established member stakes a bond on its behalf, forfeited if the newcomer cheats. Forging a thousand fake identities then requires a thousand sponsors risking real capital, so attack cost scales with the attack itself. Each new voyage into the network leaves an echo on its sponsor's reputation, and like saffron, trust stays expensive because it cannot be counterfeited cheaply.
